items.title: Black Sea LPG carrier sinks; second merchant vessel lost off Bulgaria in two days
items.summary: Bulgarian authorities confirmed that LPG carrier GAS HUSKY sank on November 17, after another cargo ship sank nearby on November 16. Maritime-industry reporting says all 19 GAS HUSKY crew members were rescued. A drone strike is alleged by a security firm, but the cause is not yet officially confirmed and wider energy-shipping disruption is unverified.

observations.label: November 17 incident
observations.value: GAS HUSKY sank about 50 nautical miles off Bulgaria; emergency beacon reportedly activated at 08:02 local time; ship en route Alexandria to Midia

observations.label: November 16 incident
observations.value: Second vessel, general cargo ship, sank nearby; earlier rescue of its 12 crew confirmed

observations.label: Casualty and physical-flow distinction
observations.value: AP reported rescue operation under way; later Seatrade Maritime reported all 19 gas-carrier crew rescued; vessel loss confirmed, regional supply effect not established

observations.label: Cause and next checks
observations.value: Drone involvement attributed by maritime-security firm but not confirmed by Bulgaria; monitor official investigation, port disruptions, cargo losses and war-risk premiums

items.key_finding: Two documented vessel sinkings elevate Black Sea shipping risk without yet proving a regional LPG supply shock.

sources.title: Associated Press November 17: Gas carrier sinks off Bulgaria
Seatrade Maritime November 17: Both sinkings and rescue updates

items.title: US optical networking shares rally on proposed China equipment import restrictions
items.summary: Reuters reports that US officials intend to advance proposed limits on importing Chinese optical transceivers despite objections from major technology buyers. Coherent, Lumentum and Applied Optoelectronics rallied in premarket trading. US suppliers could benefit, but the ban is not yet enacted and capacity shortages may delay data-center buildouts.

observations.label: November 17 premarket market moves
observations.value: COHR +11.3%, LITE +8.2% in pre-open market report; AAOI +8.1% at 08:06 ET; indicative intraday/pre-open observations, not closes

observations.label: Regulatory catalyst
observations.value: Reuters November 17 06:02 ET: Administration intends to advance FCC restrictions on imports of newer Chinese optical-transceiver models; still proposed, not final

observations.label: Company fundamentals
observations.value: AAOI Q3 revenue $269.9M, data-center revenue $155.6M versus $43.9M prior-year; company warns grid-power constraints may delay 2027 US capacity expansion

observations.label: Risks and invalidation
observations.value: Final rule scope, customer opposition, supplier capacity, optical component costs, delivery lead times and actual hyperscaler orders; regulatory retreat or prolonged manufacturing bottlenecks weaken thesis

items.key_finding: A prospective policy shift sparked sector-specific strength in optical networking, with execution capacity the main bottleneck.

sources.title: Reuters November 17: China data-center equipment curb advances
Barron's November 17 premarket optical stock moves
Applied Optoelectronics Q3 financial results / SEC filing

items.title: Similarweb gains premarket after profit beat and third full-year guidance increase
items.summary: Similarweb's third-quarter revenue rose 16% to $83.0 million and it raised full-year guidance to $318-$320 million. Large-customer retention and contracted backlog improved while shares rose about 17.5% premarket. Sustained cash conversion and retention remain key tests of the AI-related enterprise demand narrative.

observations.label: November 17 premarket
observations.value: SMWB approximately +17.5% premarket near 09:30 ET; not a close

observations.label: Q3 financials
observations.value: Revenue $83.0M (+16% YoY); non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.10; GAAP operating profit $3.1M

observations.label: Quality of revenue
observations.value: Large-account net retention 114% versus 105% year earlier; remaining performance obligations $334.2M (+25% YoY)

observations.label: Forward guidance and risks
observations.value: FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $318M-$320M; monitor enterprise renewals, operating margins, normalized free cash flow and customer concentration; weak retention would undermine thesis

items.key_finding: SMWB's revenue growth, improved retention and higher guidance support its premarket move more convincingly than a sentiment-only rally.

sources.title: Similarweb November 17 Q3 results via Business Wire
Investing.com November 17 earnings reaction and guidance

items.title: UKMTO updates Hormuz tanker warning: reported second strike, crew unaccounted for
items.summary: UKMTO's update to warning 208 reports a second strike on a tanker near Khasab, Oman, and says crew are currently unaccounted for, reversing an earlier safe-crew report. Reuters meanwhile reports recovering Middle East oil exports and stable early crude prices. Neither casualties nor a sustained cargo-flow loss have been independently verified.

observations.label: UKMTO warning 208 update
observations.value: Update 001 timestamp 17 Nov 07:45 UTC; reported second strike; crew status unaccounted for; damage unknown

observations.label: Early November 17 crude snapshot at 09:10 GMT
observations.value: Brent $92.61/bbl (+0.2%); WTI $85.73/bbl nearly flat; intraday, not settlement

observations.label: Physical-flow evidence
observations.value: Reuters reports recovering Middle East shipments; no independently verified incremental oil export losses

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Vessel/crew verification, cargo status, UKMTO/MARAD updates, Hormuz transits, insurance rates and Brent/WTI/XLE/XOP; verified export disruption would overturn supply-recovery case

items.key_finding: The reported second tanker strike worsens security risk without yet demonstrating sustained oil-flow disruption.

sources.title: Reuters November 17 oil-price and export report

items.title: Red Cat plunges premarket after withdrawing full-year revenue target
items.summary: Red Cat withdrew its 2026 revenue target after slower contract funding and awards, despite reporting quarterly revenue growth. Premarket shares fell sharply. Cash holdings provide a buffer, but timing and conversion of defense procurement into funded revenue are uncertain.

observations.label: November 16 company results
observations.value: Q3 revenue $11.8M (+22% YoY); cash $242.7M; full-year 2026 revenue outlook withdrawn

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Procurement awards, customer deliveries, burn rate and inventory; funded contract conversion could improve outlook

items.key_finding: Revenue guidance withdrawal points to real execution and funding risk behind RCAT's premarket repricing.

sources.title: Red Cat third-quarter results and withdrawn outlook
